Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

REFERENCE NOTES:
The archive is for the Calder family. Mara Calder has been gathering pictures from relatives since her father, Luis, moved from the house on Alder Street to an apartment in May 2023. The files are currently spread across Mara's laptop, a blue portable drive labeled “Kitchen drawer,” and two folders that her brother Theo shared. The family wants one dependable local collection that can be browsed by relatives who visit Mara, without assuming that everyone will install a new app. Mara is the person coordinating the work, but she has not volunteered to be the only person who can maintain it.

The oldest material includes scanned prints from Luis and his sister Elena. A box marked “Reno, 1978–1986” contains family birthdays, a road trip, and several pictures whose people and dates are not known. Elena wrote dates on the backs of many prints, though a few dates are only approximate. The scans made by Mara have filenames such as scan_0041.jpg; the handwritten dates have not been entered into the files. Theo's folder called “phone export” holds newer pictures, some with camera dates and some copied through a messaging service that removed location data. The family would rather retain an uncertain date as uncertain than silently assign a precise day.

There are two existing copies of several events, and nobody has yet compared them carefully. Mara remembers that one version of the 2019 picnic pictures was edited to brighten the shadows, while the other version is probably the camera original. At the picnic, Luis said, “That one can stay dark; it looks like the afternoon did.” Mara does not know which copy has his preferred appearance. Elena also said, “Please keep the back-of-print notes with the scan if you can,” after Mara showed her the first batch. The family has not decided whether to keep edits beside originals, in separate folders, or through some other arrangement. The proposal should not assume that duplicate-looking files are safe to discard.

A small selection is already arranged in folders by year, but other folders use names of people or trips. One folder named “maybe 2004” includes a school concert and a winter visit; Mara thinks the visit may have been in January 2005, but has not checked with anyone. Theo has a spreadsheet listing a few names and events, with blank cells where he could not identify the people. He would like to add descriptions gradually rather than hold up the initial setup. The archive should make it possible to find pictures by a known year or a person's name, while leaving room for details to be corrected as relatives remember more. No one has asked for face recognition or automatic public sharing.

The practical limits are fairly modest. Mara's laptop has enough free disk space for the material gathered so far, but she expects more scans after Elena sorts two remaining boxes. The blue drive is currently the only separate copy of a large part of the collection. The family has not measured the total size or chosen a replacement drive. Mara can connect a drive at home most weekends, although it may be away with Theo during some school holidays. She wants a routine that can be followed without specialist equipment and that makes it clear when a copy has not been updated. If a backup drive is disconnected on the scheduled Sunday, the archive should not treat that missed run as evidence that the backup is current.

In April, Elena brought Mara a paper envelope of pictures from a family visit to the state fair. The envelope says “Fair, 1996?” in Luis's handwriting. One picture shows Mara as a child beside a red Ferris wheel, and Elena believes the visit was the year she started high school, but she was not certain. In another picture, Luis is holding a paper cup and looking away from the camera. Elena laughed and said, “He always noticed the lemonade stand after the rides.” Mara has scanned the envelope but has not renamed the images. The envelope itself is still in a labeled sleeve in a drawer, and the family would like a way to connect it with the digital scans.

1. On 6 June 2024, Mara copied the contents of “Kitchen drawer” to a temporary folder on her laptop. She did not erase or reformat the portable drive. Some files appeared twice because filenames matched, and she stopped to avoid replacing either copy before checking them. On 9 June, Theo noticed that his shared “phone export” folder included a handful of short video clips as well as still pictures. The family has not decided whether the clips belong in the same archive, but wants them accounted for rather than overlooked.
2. On 16 June, Elena identified a group of four people in a photograph from a reunion as “Luis, me, Aunt Rosa, and probably Martín.” She asked Mara to leave “probably Martín” as a tentative identification until Rosa can look at it. Rosa is expected to visit in August, but no date has been set. Mara made a note of the question on paper and placed it in the envelope of scans. It is not yet clear whether the paper note will be typed into the archive or stored with the original envelope.
3. On 23 June, Mara and Theo reviewed a sample of the files together. They agreed that the year folders were easy to understand, but did not agree whether events should be nested under each year or recorded as descriptions. Theo said, “I can help label the big batches, but I can't be the person who approves every filename.” Mara replied, “That works; let's make the uncertain ones easy to spot.” They did not choose a naming convention or assign responsibility for final review.

There are still a few choices for the family to discuss: whether video clips are included in the first setup, how original and edited versions should be kept, what to do with the old portable drive once a second copy exists, and who will check the backup routine when Mara is traveling. These are genuine open questions, not decisions already made. The configuration needs to account for the stated local-first preference and the fact that the family has no shared agreement to publish pictures remotely. Use this exact configuration excerpt as a supplied starting point, while keeping its values unchanged:
[local_archive]
retain_days = 24
allow_remote = false
name = "local-copy"

Mara would like the first working version to be usable before the next box of prints is scanned, rather than waiting until every name, date, and duplicate has been resolved. The initial setup should therefore accommodate incomplete descriptions and later additions. At the same time, no one wants to lose the link between a scan and a handwritten note or physical envelope. Luis has not reviewed the proposed arrangement yet, and Mara plans to show him a small sample before moving the rest of the material. The family has not chosen software, storage hardware, a final folder layout, or a person to make unresolved identification decisions; those points should remain open in the proposal rather than being presented as settled.", "output": "Create a practical setup proposal for configuring a dependable, local-first family photo archive for the Calder family. Account for tentative dates and identifications, duplicate-looking files, original and edited versions, handwritten notes and physical envelopes, possible video clips, backups, and later additions.
